title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Substitution Measure Set by the Guaranty in Force and the Basic Entitlement
content:
When an assuming veteran substitutes entitlement on a VA Home Loan Guaranty loan, the substitution measure (the entitlement figure from which the seller's restoration is figured) compares the guaranty in force on the loan record with the entitlement still charged to the loan (the entitlement charge entries less the restoration entries in the loan's entitlement history) and with the basic entitlement, which is 36000.00 dollars on every program.

## The measure

The substitution measure is the guaranty in force on the loan record where that guaranty is below the entitlement still charged but not below the basic entitlement; where the guaranty in force is below both the entitlement still charged and the basic entitlement, it is the basic entitlement, never more than the entitlement still charged; otherwise it is the entitlement still charged.

| Guaranty in force below the entitlement still charged | Guaranty in force at or above 36000.00 | Substitution measure |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | The guaranty in force |
| Yes | No | The basic entitlement, 36000.00, but never more than the entitlement still charged |
| No | Either | The entitlement still charged |

## Cases (hypothetical)

| Entitlement still charged | Guaranty in force on the loan record | Substitution measure |
|---|---|---|
| 72,000.00 | 54,000.00 | 54,000.00 |
| 72,000.00 | 36,000.00 | 36,000.00 (equal to the basic entitlement, so not below it) |
| 72,000.00 | 30,000.00 | 36,000.00 |
| 33,000.00 | 30,000.00 | 33,000.00 (the basic entitlement, held to the entitlement still charged) |
| 72,000.00 | 72,000.00 | 72,000.00 (not below the entitlement still charged) |
